title: An antigen microarray protocol for COVID-19 serological analysis
author: Longworth, Dittmar
materials: TBS, Tris Buffered Saline, 10× Solution, pH 7.4

steps.title: Print antigen microarrays on slide
steps.instruction: Using a Nanoplotter 2.1, non‑contact print a 64‑array format onto nitrocellulose‑backed microscope slides; each array contains 64 spots representing a panel of 20 SARS‑CoV‑2 antigens (envelope, nucleocapsid, spike, spike fragments S1, S2, NTD, RBD, four HCoV‑229E/NL63/HKU1/OC43 S1 proteins, SARS‑CoV‑1 RBD, and variant fragments of B.1.1.7 and B.1.351). Spot each antigen in triplicate at three dilution points.

steps.title: Prepare positive and negative serum pools
steps.instruction: Pool representative positive patient sera to make a positive control pool and pool multiple negative patient sera to make a negative control pool; aliquot 100 µL of each pool and store at –20 °C (or –80 °C for long‑term storage). Ensure pools are valid controls for the experiment.

steps.title: Optional: Reconstitute normalized human serum
steps.instruction: Reconstitute pre‑2019 normalized human serum and dispense 50 µL aliquots for use as an additional control.

steps.title: Prepare serum sample plate
steps.instruction: Create a sample plate in a 384‑well deep‑well plate (Corning Cat#3342) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Using a 16‑channel pipette, add 190 µL TBS‑T + 10 % FBS to the first eight odd‑numbered columns.
Add 10 µL negative‑pool serum to wells of row M; mix gently by pipetting up‑and‑down 5×.
Add 10 µL positive‑pool serum to wells of row N; mix gently 5×.
Add 10 µL normalized human serum to wells of row O; mix gently 5×.
Add up to 96 test serum samples (10 µL each) to rows A‑L; mix gently 5× (use an 8‑channel pipette rotated as shown in Fig 3 if needed).
Seal the plate with aluminum‑foil tape.
Pause point: store the prepared plate at –20 °C for up to 3 months (or at 4 °C if used the same day) to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Block antigen microarrays for each Ig
steps.instruction: For each immunoglobulin (IgG, IgA, IgM) use a separate antigen microarray slide placed in a quadriPERM® 4‑slide plate and perform the following blocking sequence:

substeps.instruction: Add 4.5 mL TBS‑T to the slide chamber; rock gently for 30 min.
Remove TBS‑T.
Add 4.5 mL Print Buffer containing 10 % FBS; rock gently for 30 min.
Remove Print Buffer.
Add 4.5 mL TBS‑T + 10 % FBS; rock gently for 60 min.

steps.title: Attach ProPlate to microarray slide
steps.instruction: Attach a 64‑well ProPlate to each blocked slide and add incubation buffer:

substeps.instruction: Remove the slide from the blocking plate.
Place the ProPlate on the slide, aligning nitrocellulose pads with the ProPlate wells; keep the slide tab at the upper‑right corner.
Add spring clips to secure alignment.
Insert the slide‑ProPlate assembly into the ProPlate tray, maintaining the tab at the top‑right.
Using a 16‑channel pipette, add 40 µL TBS‑T + 10 % FBS to each well.

steps.title: Incubate slides with serum samples
steps.instruction: Incubate each slide with serum samples under the following conditions:

substeps.instruction: If the sample plate was frozen, thaw at 4 °C.
Transfer 10 µL of each sample (four columns per slide) from the prepared sample plate onto the corresponding wells of the slide.
Seal the slide with aluminum‑foil tape.
Incubate on a rocker at room temperature with gentle agitation for 3 h.
Return the sample plate to –20 °C unless the remaining slides are processed immediately.

steps.title: Wash slides after serum incubation
steps.instruction: Perform three successive washes to remove unbound serum:

substeps.instruction: Using a 16‑channel pipette set to 100 µL, aspirate the bulk of fluid from each well.
Add 50 µL TBS‑T to each well, mix by pipetting 25 µL up‑and‑down three times; repeat this wash three times total.
Aspirate the bulk fluid again.
Remove the ProPlate and place the slide back into a quadriPERM® 4‑slide plate.
Add 4.5 mL TBS‑T, rock gently for 3 min; repeat this TBS‑T wash once more.
Add 4.5 mL TBS‑T + 10 % FBS, rock gently for 3 min.

steps.title: Stain with fluorescent detection antibody
steps.instruction: Detect bound antibodies with a fluorophore‑conjugated secondary antibody:

substeps.instruction: Prepare detection antibody solution by adding 30 µL of the selected detection antibody (IgG, IgM or IgA) to 12 mL TBS‑T + 10 % FBS.
Add 4 mL of this solution to each slide well; rock gently at room temperature for 30 min protected from light.
Remove antibody solution.
Add 4 mL TBS‑T; remove.
Add 4 mL TBS‑T, incubate on rocker for 3 min; remove.
Add 4 mL TBS, incubate on rocker for 3 min; remove.
Transfer slides to a 50 mL tube, gently fill with ddH₂O, invert 5 times.
Remove slides carefully, avoid touching microarrays, and blow‑dry with a gentle nitrogen stream.
Pause point: scan immediately or store slides in the dark at 4 °C (up to 7 days) before scanning.

steps.title: Dry and scan microarray slides
steps.instruction: After nitrogen drying, scan each slide on an InnoScan 710 IR scanner (or equivalent) using the appropriate gain (default gain = 50) and collect fluorescence intensity data.

steps.title: Process data with Shiny analysis tool
steps.instruction: Analyze the scanned data using the AntigenMicroarray Shiny application:

substeps.instruction: Install the Shiny app following the GitHub instructions (https://github.com/JosephLongworth/AntigenMicroarray).
Upload a new slide dataset: provide the antigen names table, the print design file, and the slide quantification file (Mapix or Genepix format).
Specify slide name, sample‑plate name, detection immunoglobulin (e.g., IgG), and the intensity metric (e.g., f785_median_b785).
Click “Process Import Data” to fit supercurves and obtain gain‑normalized intensities (gain = 50).
Optionally, append additional slide datasets using the “Append” function to build a full dataset.
To reuse previously fitted data, select “Previously Fitted Data Upload”, load the file, process, and append to the current dataset as needed.
